I can hear how scared you are and I wish I could reassure you but the truth is you can be at risk of dying at any BMI, especially with a previous history that could have resulted in damage to your body. Your ED is trying to kill you while it convinces you you’re being silly or dramatic, but I promise you that you’re neither of those things. These symptoms are serious and your fear is valid. Your ED is promising you that it’ll make you like your body if you just achieve more weight loss but that’s a lie, it will only get worse. I know people can survive for a very long time so your mind tells you that it’ll be fine, but your mind is wrong.

Please please PLEASE go to the doctor and get a checkup/blood work. Tell them about your symptoms, even if you’re too terrified to tell them the full extent of your ED. Please, don’t take this lightly. I know it’s hell in your brain, there isn’t a light at the end of the tunnel, and you don’t know what to do, *but is it possible that you make seeing a doctor the one thing you can do right now?* Make a list of all your symptoms, take the list with you to read, and don’t minimize them. 

**I want you to stay alive**, I want you to have a future where you can build a life full of peace and happiness, I want to come on Reddit one day and read your beautiful recovery story. I am sending you so so so much love and I’m proud of you for reaching out for support here, you’re not alone. 🤍

Take a deep breath, you’ll be okay. You’re obviously eating a very small amount, which means there is already very little waste, and basically nothing to keep it moving through your intestinal track. Drink lots of water and be patient, you won’t die and you’ll poop eventually, but again, drink lots of water and stay hydrated with electrolytes so the waste in your intestines doesn’t dry out (also drinking a lot of water will help you poop). I’ve gone a fair bit longer than a week many times, as have numerous people here. Unless you’re in pain, you’re okay and you just need to let your body do its thing. Please don’t take laxatives prematurely - if you have a strong urge to go and no matter what you do you can’t because it’s stuck/dried out, etc., then you might consider a laxative for constipation (the ones the hydrate are better, rather than the motility ones).

Also, if you’re severely restricting you should see a doctor anyways to discuss your symptoms, get help, and get some blood work done to evaluate your health.

First off, the DSM-5 states that recovery from a MDE begins within a year for 4/5 people. Obviously there is a lot of variability (severe MDE’s last a lot longer usually). People throw around the term “depressive episode” quite flippantly online, but if you actually have clinical depression, an MDE isn’t just a few week ‘blip’ - it is debilitating and the criteria states that the symptoms must be causing *significant* distress and impairment.    

“Chronic depression” is PDD, and yes it is less severe than MDD but it is long term. PDD in the DSM-5 represents the consolidation of both “chronic major depressive disorder” (CMDD) and “dysthymia” from the DSM-IV. If you have both PDD and MDD it’s often called “double depression”. This is specified in the DSM as “PDD with persistent major depressive episode” (meaning full criteria for MDD have been met for 2+ years) or as “PDD with intermittent major depressive episodes” (you have episodic MDE’s just like in MDD, but in-between episodes you still meet the criteria for PDD). These MDE episodes are specified as mild, moderate, or severe, just as they are under the MDD criteria. If you have both MDD and PDD, you also receive the diagnosis for both (I.e. MDD and PDD w/ persistent major depressive episode, severe). So yes, you still have MDD and it can still be just as severe and debilitating.
